grh_4c0ada8643f5381953d6.title: Susan Comes Marching Home
paragraphs: Riverâ€™s End welcomes home Army nurse Susan Anderson, who has survived wartime service and years in a Japanese prison camp. Susan has only thirty days of leave before returning to duty, and she has already decided what she wants most: to marry Hillary Dana, the shy lumber-mill owner she has loved since their school days. Hillary loves Susan too, but feels inadequate beside a decorated Army captain and is so painfully bashful that every attempt to propose collapses into comic disaster. Dr. Christian and Judy repeatedly try to coach him, but even a carefully rehearsed visit ends with a broken goldfish bowl and Hillary fleeing without his hat. Convinced he has made a fool of himself, Hillary retreats to a fishing cabin he had quietly begun building for Susan after wartime reports made him fear she would never come home. Susan finds him there, forces the truth into the open and accepts his clumsy proposal. Dr. Christian arrives with one more piece of good news: the Army is releasing personnel who spent more than sixty days in prison camps, so Susanâ€™s discharge will allow the couple to begin their life together without another separation.

The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Ray Appleby as writer and Bob Anderson as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_4c98187aad631b83885b.title: The Panther
paragraphs: A young frontier woman traveling home through a forest ignores warnings that a large panther has been killing livestock in the area. As darkness closes in and the animal stalks her, she takes refuge in an abandoned house, only to have the panther force its way inside. She retreats upstairs and finally into the attic, dragging a heavy trunk across the trap door while the animal repeatedly hurls itself against the weakening barrier. Just as her strength and the hinges are giving out, help arrives below. More than a century later, her descendant remembers the ordeal whenever he drives past the modern highway interchange built over the site where his great-great-grandmother fought for her life.

Other credited names include Elliott Lewis as director, Elliott Lewis as producer, Percy Grainger as writer, and Lorne Greene as host.

grh_4c397f9a59cabe331359.title: Revenge at Harness Creek
paragraphs: After young Lex Harcourt is killed by Adam Robey, Lex's brother, Sheriff Cash Harcourt, becomes determined to settle the matter with vengeance rather than a trial. Robey claims Lex drew first and agrees to surrender only if Britt will deliver him to the district marshal at Standish Falls. Cash catches them on the trail and prepares to kill Robey, but Britt stands unarmed between the two men and makes Cash face the fact that revenge would require murdering a friend as well. Cash cannot pull the trigger and gives up his gun, allowing Britt to take Robey in for a lawful trial.

paragraphs: Cowboy star Buck Houston enters Blair with disabling sciatica that has no physical cause, and Kildare discovers the pain is tied to the older actor's resentment and guilt over living behind a manufactured Western hero persona.
